result.markdown: --- title: "Latent space DyNAMs with position-rate link" author: - name: "Alberto Caimo" - name: "Isabella Gollini" format: html: fontsize: 1.1em grid: body-width: 850px margin-width: 400px embed-resources: true theme: - flatly - custom.css --- ::: {.cell} ::: ```{=html} ``` This vignette shows the main functions of **ls.dynam** on simulated data. The model and the methods are described in Caimo and Gollini (2026), *Latent space dynamic network actor models with position-rate link*. ## Model specification In a dynamic network actor model (DyNAM) each event is the outcome of two decisions: when an actor becomes active, and whom it selects. Actor $i$ becomes active with intensity $$\lambda_i(t) = \exp\{\xi^\top s(i;t) + a_i\},$$ and selects receiver $j \neq i$ with probability proportional to $\exp\{\zeta^\top s(i,j;t) + u_i^\top v_j\}$, where $u_i$ and $v_j$ are latent sender and receiver positions. The choice model identifies the positions only up to transformations, but it identifies the *latent popularity* $\pi_i$, how much the average sender favours $i$ as a receiver, and the *excess self-affinity* $\rho_i$, the preference of $i$ for actors like itself beyond its popularity (`position_summaries()`). The position-rate link relates them to the activity effects: $$a_i \sim N\{\mu_a + g_\pi(\pi_i) + g_\rho(\rho_i), \sigma_a^2\},$$ with natural cubic splines $g_\pi$ and $g_\rho$. Inference is modular: the positions are estimated from the choice of receivers alone, and the link is estimated given them. ## Simulated data We simulate $M = 3{,}000$ events among $n = 40$ actors, with $D = 1$ latent dimension and activity associated with latent popularity only. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ls.dynam) n <- 40; D <- 1 f <- function(x) 1.5 * (plogis(3 * x) - 0.5) # a smooth curve tr <- make_truth(n = n, D = D, link_fun = list(pop = f, rho = NULL), link_var = c("pop", "rho"), mean_u = 1, sigma_a = 0.5, xi = c(rate_indeg = 0.1), zeta = c(choice_recip = 0.5), seed = 1) ev <- simulate_lsdynam(tr$theta, n = n, M = 3000, seed = 2) head(ev, 3) #> time sender receiver #> 1 0.03284149 31 30 #> 2 0.06311876 40 26 #> 3 0.08786836 22 30 ``` ::: ## Estimation `lsdynam_fit()` fits both stages. By default the statistics are the in-degree in the rate sub-process and reciprocity in the choice sub-process, and the link is the additive link in latent popularity and excess self-affinity. Here we use the Laplace approximation (`inference = "map"`), which takes seconds; the analysis in the paper uses posterior simulation (see below). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fit <- lsdynam_fit(ev, n = n, D = D, inference = "map", n_starts = 3, verbose = FALSE) summary(fit) #> Latent space DyNAM: n = 40 actors, M = 3000 events, D = 1 #> Inference: choice module laplace, rate module laplace #> Link: pop + rho (spline); sigma_a = 0.457 (eb), sigma_kappa = 1.000 (fixed) #> #> Coefficients (posterior mean, sd and 95% credible interval): #> mean sd lower upper #> xi[rate_indeg] 0.1040 0.0201 0.0651 0.142 #> zeta[choice_recip] 0.4600 0.0396 0.3880 0.541 #> mu_a 0.0790 0.0982 -0.1130 0.270 #> kappa[pop_1] 0.1070 0.1570 -0.1890 0.410 #> kappa[pop_2] 0.4850 0.1110 0.2730 0.701 #> kappa[pop_3] 0.1710 0.1510 -0.1300 0.457 #> kappa[pop_4] 0.3900 0.0923 0.2080 0.570 #> kappa[rho_1] 0.0182 0.1510 -0.2780 0.296 #> kappa[rho_2] -0.0304 0.0993 -0.2260 0.168 #> kappa[rho_3] 0.0285 0.1240 -0.2100 0.266 #> kappa[rho_4] -0.0436 0.1060 -0.2520 0.158 #> #> Contrasts of the components (level at the 90% minus level at the 10% quantile): #> x_10 x_90 mean lower upper prob_positive #> pop -1.180 1.30 1.750 1.260 2.20 1.00 #> rho -0.345 1.15 -0.192 -0.819 0.45 0.27 #> R2 of the link: 0.625 #> #> Log Bayes factors: #> log_bf_savage_dickey log_bf_laplace #> link 13.80 13.10 #> pop | rho 19.30 18.80 #> rho | pop -8.83 -8.75 ``` ::: The contrasts compare the level of each component at the 90% and 10% quantiles of its summary, and the log Bayes factors test the whole link and each component given the other. `plot()` shows the components of the link; the rug marks the actors' values. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(fit) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](ls.dynam_files/figure-html/link-plot-1.png){width=100%} ::: ::: The truth is a step in popularity and no effect of excess self-affinity. The contrasts and Bayes factors can also be obtained directly: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ct <- link_contrast(fit, "pop") round(c(estimate = ct$mean, lower = ct$ci[1], upper = ct$ci[2]), 2) #> estimate lower upper #> 1.75 1.26 2.20 # excess self-affinity given popularity link_evidence(fit, components = "rho")$log_bf10_laplace #> [1] -8.749341 ``` ::: Links in other summaries can be compared on the same positions by their log marginal likelihoods; the difference between `"pop + rho"` and `"pop"` is the log Bayes factor for excess self-affinity given popularity. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cmp <- link_comparison_table(fit, list("pop + rho" = c("pop", "rho"), pop = "pop", rho = "rho", r = "r")) cmp$table[, c("link", "K", "sigma_a", "log_ml_vs_M1", "R2")] #> link K sigma_a log_ml_vs_M1 R2 #> 1 pop + rho 8 0.4572894 2.8926957 0.62465963 #> 2 pop 4 0.4337551 11.7227970 0.65843943 #> 3 rho 4 0.7395515 -6.2166191 -0.01230219 #> 4 r 4 0.6232275 -0.5346441 0.28485946 ``` ::: With one dimension the positions can be displayed. Filled points have positive self-affinity. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_positions(fit, ellipses = FALSE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](ls.dynam_files/figure-html/positions-1.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ## Prediction The models are compared on held-out events: $\mathcal{M}_0$ has no latent positions, $\mathcal{M}_1$ has positions but no link, and $\mathcal{M}_2$ has both. The choice score compares $\mathcal{M}_1$ with $\mathcal{M}_0$, the rate score $\mathcal{M}_2$ with $\mathcal{M}_1$. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_tr <- 2400 train <- ev[seq_len(m_tr), ] m0 <- lsdynam_fit(train, n = n, D = 0, inference = "map", verbose = FALSE) m2 <- lsdynam_fit(train, n = n, D = 1, inference = "map", verbose = FALSE) m1 <- lsdynam_fit(train, n = n, D = 1, link = "none", inference = "map", choice = m2$choice, verbose = FALSE) sc <- lapply(list(M0 = m0, M1 = m1, M2 = m2), predictive_scores, events_full = ev, n = n, m_train = m_tr, n_draws = 100) rbind("M1 - M0" = score_difference(sc$M1, sc$M0)[2, 2:4], "M2 - M1" = score_difference(sc$M2, sc$M1)[1, 2:4]) #> units difference se #> M1 - M0 600 404.315987 24.8857022 #> M2 - M1 40 2.044529 0.8838632 ``` ::: The latent positions improve the prediction of the receivers considerably. The link improves the rate score only slightly, because the rate of an actor who has sent many events is determined by its own record: it describes how activity varies with position rather than improving the forecast of when actors send. ## Posterior simulation The analysis of the paper simulates both modules with a Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm (MALA), from many starting configurations of the choice module, and adds the cut posterior. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fit <- lsdynam_fit(ev, n = n, D = D, n_iter = 12000, burn_in = 2000, thin = 5, n_starts = 10, n_cut = The analysis of the paper used the second fifth of the observation period and the actors who both send and receive in it. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ev <- read_konect_events("out.radoslaw_email_email") ev <- prepare_events(ev) ev <- select_time_window(ev, start_frac = 0.2, end_frac = 0.4) fa <- filter_active_both(ev) fit <- lsdynam_fit(fa$events_df, n = fa$n, D = 2, n_iter = 12000, burn_in = 2000, thin = 5, n_starts = 30, n_cut = 300) ``` :::
